script: Getting the compensation memo. No staff or non-exempt position is approved, and no requisition goes forward, without Compensation's pre-search memo. So get it first.
Start with the position description. Use the standard Vanderbilt position description template.

Next, request the review from V U Compensation. Send the position description with the Vacant Reclassification or New Position Request Form, for a new or vacant position, or the Filled Reclassification Request Form, for a filled position. Send them to the Compensation team, at V U dot compensation at Vanderbilt dot E D U. New positions are requested through V U Compensation, not your engagement consultant.
Include the work location. The recommended pay range depends on it. Say if the role is in New York, Miami, California, or on another campus. Don't let it default to Nashville.

Compensation reviews market data and internal equity, matches the duties to a job in the job architecture, and sends the memo. It gives you the six-digit job code, the job name and level, the assignment category, and the recommended pay range. A reclassification gets a reclass memo instead.
Use the memo to build the position. Enter the job code, name, and category from the memo, and attach the memo to the position. Central HR won't approve a staff position without it.

Attach it to the requisition too. Central recruiting checks that the memo is from the last twelve months, and that its job code matches the requisition. If your business unit doesn't want hiring managers to see the full range, send the memo to central recruiting directly instead.
Two things to remember. VTS temporary positions don't need a memo. And a memo older than twelve months means a new request.
